text:
omar: Seeing a spike in fncall validation rejects on the canary starting ~09:46 UTC. Rejects x6 and most are being routed to degen fallback which is blowing up unit cost. Console sampling is almost zero so we can't inspect payloads.

jess: Canary only? Any customer impact or just metrics? :eyes:

omar: Canary only for now. No customer reports, but the routing churn is concerning. Need samples + quick telemetry.

ben: I shipped validators:v2.4.0-canary with a stricter union->array coercion flag earlier today. That was intended to catch malformed tool responses.

claire: That aligns with my deploy notes. The stricter flag should have been limited to canary but still might be too aggressive for some adapters.

omar: Example sanitized log line: ```[09:47:12Z] route=fncall-eu-canary model=open-7b-q4 validator=validators:v2.4.0-canary outcome=REJECT reason="attachments expected array, got string"```

omar: Small payloads, not huge prompts. Many rejects are hard not soft.

jess: Console only shows aggregate rejects. Can we add a short-lived panel that breaks down reject_count by validator_version + route + fallback_route and sample_rate? Need to correlate.

ben: I can push validators:v2.4.1 with a soft-mode toggle and an endpoint to backfill raw (redacted) samples. Requesting sample override: route=fncall-eu-canary event=reject sample=100% duration=15m. This will flow to S3 via the redact pipeline.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: starting roll validators:v2.4.1 -> canary (owner: @ben)

jess: Approve sample override for 15m. Enable s3-redact pipeline and add audit note. :white_check_mark:

product: product: We can't let canary fallbacks create billing or capacity surprises. Suggest a console-level "shadow-fallback" toggle that routes to an observability-only path (no billing, no quota consumption) while still surfacing metrics.

ben: Agree. I'll implement routing_tag=routing.shadow for that path and emit metrics: validation.reject_mode={hard,soft,coerced} and routing.fallback_type={shadow,real}. Also add a histogram for fallback_cost_estimate to quantify impact.

claire: For the temporary dashboard include an inspector that will show redacted payload + model reply + validator fingerprint hash. That helps pinpoint whether adapters are returning wrong shapes or model outputs are malformed.

omar: Also, can we change default canary behavior to shadow-fallback? If validators reject and fallback would normally route to degen, instead shadow it unless product explicitly disables. Reduces billing noise during rollouts.

product: product: OK to default canaries to shadow-fallback. Expose a console toggle per-rollout. Add a small warning banner showing when shadow is active.

ben: Plan of action: 1) enable 100% sample override for 15m 2) deploy validators:v2.4.1 with soft-mode toggle 3) add dashboard panel + inspector 4) implement shadow-fallback routing_tag and ensure billing pipeline ignores shadowed fallbacks 5) backfill samples and triage

alert-bot: alert-bot: created incident INC-2026-402 "canary-validator-rejects spike" (owner: eng-platform)

jess: Ben/Omar please post 2-3 redacted samples in this thread when available. Claire, can you add a quick runbook step to revert adapter vs revert validator depending on sample content? Keep it short.

claire: Will do. Revert guidance: if adapter produces wrong Content-Type or structure revert adapter. If root cause is model producing text in wrong shape, revert validator strictness and open eval to capture examples.

omar: Will share redacted examples as soon as S3 backfill completes. Also checking whether our telemetry double-counts events when shadow-fallback enabled; we must avoid misreporting billing metrics.

ben: I'll add a switch in telemetry ingestion that marks shadowed events as non-billable and ensures they don't increment real billing aggregations.

jess: Thanks team. Keep comms tight, update incident with links to dashboard and two redacted examples. :thumbsup:
